### Observed differences

- The two activity blocks swapped their place in the trace. In the earlier window, A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 appeared early (mean positions about 0.31–0.36 of the trace) and A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 appeared late (about 0.63); in the later window, A20–A25 appear at about 0.39–0.40 and A19/A23/A26–A28 at about 0.66–0.71. All of these activities occur in roughly the same share of traces in both windows, so this is not a participation effect. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011]
- The order between the blocks and A29/A33 flipped. Before, A29 preceded A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 in about 99 in 100 traces; in the later window, each of these activities precedes A29 in about 97–98 in 100 traces, and the same flip holds against A33 (A33 preceded A20 in about 995 of 1000 traces before; A20 precedes A33 in about 995 of 1000 after). [REL016, REL022, REL028, REL037, REL042, REL017, REL023, REL029, REL038, REL043]
- Cross-block pairs flipped as well: for example, A23 preceded A20 in about 21 in 100 traces containing both before, while in the later window A20 precedes A23 in about 21 in 100; the same reversal appears for A21, A22, A24 and A25 against A23 and A26–A28, and A19 moved from before to after A20–A25, A29 and A33. [REL012, REL018, REL024, REL030, REL031, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011]
- Successors swapped accordingly. Before, A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 led almost exclusively to A29 (93–100% of their observed outgoing transitions); in the later window they lead to A34 (90–100%). Conversely, A20–A25 lost A34 as a successor (previously about 13–26% of their outgoing transitions) and gained A29 (about 17–24%). [DIR003, DIR007, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR008, DIR009]
- A33 and A44 now feed the opposite block: A33's outgoing transitions moved from A20–A25 (about 15–27% each) to A19/A23/A26–A28 (about 16–23% each), and A44's moved from A06 and A19/A23/A26–A28 to A20–A25 (about 14–25% each). A29 and A33 themselves occur later (mean positions about 0.36 to 0.48 and 0.54 to 0.67). [DIR013, DIR014, POS012, POS013]
- A06 became rarer and rewired: it appears in about 12 in 100 traces in the later window versus about 30 in 100 before (mean occurrences per trace 0.32 to 0.13), and its outgoing transitions shifted from mainly A23, A28, A27, A19 and A26 to mainly A48, A16, A50 and A15; its feeder edge from A44 (about 26% of A44's outgoing transitions before) nearly disappeared. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR014, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the block A20, A21, A22, A24, A25 executes before A29 and A33, while the block A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 executes after them — the two blocks swapped their order around A29 and A33, and the handover into A34 now comes from the second block instead of the first. This rests on direct relational evidence (near-total order flips for every cross-block pair and against A29/A33), agreeing positional shifts of about 0.24 earlier and 0.35 later in opposite directions, and consistent successor changes (the A29↔A34 handover swap, A33 and A44 retargeting to the opposite block). Screening produced 93 qualifying items against about 1 expected without change, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a modification of the process from a flipped mix of two pre-existing execution variants; the lag-based items mostly rest on a single observation in one window and add little support; A34's own position was not measured directly. [REL016, REL017, REL012, POS003, POS002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR013, DIR014]

Other differences: A06 shows a separate participation and structural change — its presence fell from about 30 to about 12 in 100 traces, and its successors changed from mainly A23/A26–A28/A19 to mainly A48/A16/A50/A15, consistent with losing its incoming edge from A44; this is not part of the block-swap hypothesis. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR014, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]

Let me work through this evidence carefully.

We have 200 traces before, 200 after. Screening: 208 units tested, 93 items qualified, 1.03 expected without change. That's a huge excess — 93 items vs about 1 expected. So the count is many times larger than chance expectation. This means the screening comparison does not lead to "insufficient evidence" — the number of items is far beyond what an unchanged process produces. So we must judge the hypothesis on directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

All items are control-flow family (OCC, DIR, POS, REL, LAG). No time (TWAIT) or resource items, so I must not discuss time or resources.

Let me characterize the main behavioural differences.

OCC001: A06 participation dropped from 30% to 12% of traces; mean occurrences per trace from 0.32 to 0.125. Support 60 before, 24 after. So A06 became much rarer.

DIR001: outgoing transitions of A06 redistributed massively (cosine dissimilarity 0.94). Before, A06's outgoing edges went mostly to A23 (0.20), A28 (0.17), A27 (0.17), A19 (0.16), A26 (0.11), A48 (0.03), A21 (0.03)... After, A06's outgoing edges go to A48 (0.24), A16 (0.24), A50 (0.12), A15 (0.08), and various small ones. Support 64 before, 25 after. So A06's successors changed completely.

DIR003: A19's outgoing: before 100% to A29; after 91% to A34 (plus small A14, A24, A45). Support 42 before, 35 after. So A19 now leads to A34 instead of A29.

DIR007: A23's outgoing: before 96% to A29; after 98% to A34. Support 47/42.

DIR010: A26's outgoing: before 93% to A29; after 90% to A34. Support 42/49.

DIR011: A27: before 98% to A29; after 100% to A34. Support 42/39.

DIR012: A28: before 97% to A29; after 98% to A34. Support 33/41.

DIR013: A33's outgoing: before to A24 (0.27), A22 (0.20), A25 (0.20), A21 (0.15), A20 (0.16); after to A26 (0.23), A28 (0.21), A23 (0.21), A27 (0.20), A19 (0.16). Support 201/200. So A33's successors changed from the {A20–A25} group to the {A19, A23, A26–A28} group.

DIR014: A44's outgoing: before to A06 (0.26), A19 (0.16), A26 (0.16), A23 (0.15), A27 (0.14), A28 (0.10); after to A24 (0.25), A21 (0.20), A20 (0.18), A25 (0.16), A22 (0.14). Support 201/202. So A44's successors changed from the {A06, A19, A23, A26–A28} group to the {A20–A25} group.

DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR008, DIR009: A20, A21, A22, A24, A25 each: before they led to A34 among others; after A34 is replaced by A29. E.g., DIR004 A20: before A34 0.24; after A29 0.18, A34 gone. DIR005 A21: before A34 0.26; after A29 0.20. DIR006 A22: before A34 0.13; after A29 0.24. DIR008 A24: before A34 0.145; after A29 0.17. DIR009 A25: before A34 0.21; after A29 0.20.

So there's a big pattern: edges into A29 before, into A34 after, for many sources (A19, A20, A21, A22, A23, A24, A25, A26, A27, A28). And A33 and A44 swapped which group they feed.

POS items: A20–A25 (POS003–POS008) moved from mean position ~0.63 to ~0.39 (earlier in traces). A29 moved from ~0.36 to ~0.48 (later). A33 moved from ~0.54 to ~0.67 (later). A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 moved from ~0.31–0.36 to ~0.66–0.71 (much later). A06 position redistributed with support drop.

REL items: Many. Key ones:

REL016 (A20, A29): before co-occur in 100% of traces, B_before_A (A29 before A20) 0.995; after co-occurrence 1.0, A_before_B (A20 before A29) 0.98. So the order between A20 and A29 flipped completely: A29 used to come before A20; now A20 comes before A29.

REL017 (A20, A33): before A33 before A20 (0.995); after A20 before A33 (0.995). Flip.

REL022 (A21, A29): flip from A29 before A21 (0.99) to A21 before A29 (0.98).

REL023 (A21, A33): flip.

REL028 (A22, A29): flip. REL029 (A22, A33): flip.

REL037 (A24, A29): flip. REL038 (A24, A33): flip.

REL042 (A25, A29): flip. REL043 (A25, A33): flip.

REL012 (A20, A23): before A23 before A20 (0.215) with A_only 0.77; after A20 before A23 (0.21) with A_only 0.79. So order flipped between A20 and A23.

REL013 (A20, A26): before A26 before A20 (0.21); after A20 before A26 (0.23). Flip.

REL014 (A20, A27): flip. REL015 (A20, A28): flip.

REL018 (A21, A23): flip. REL019 (A21, A26): flip. REL020 (A21, A27): flip. REL021 (A21, A28): flip.

REL024 (A22, A23): flip. REL025 (A22, A26): flip. REL026 (A22, A27): flip. REL027 (A22, A28): flip.

REL030 (A23, A24): before A23 before A24 (0.215); after A24 before A23 (0.205). Flip.

REL031 (A23, A25): flip. REL032 (A23, A29): flip. REL033 (A23, A33): flip.

REL034 (A24, A26): flip. REL035 (A24, A27): flip. REL036 (A24, A28): flip.

REL039 (A25, A26): flip. REL040 (A25, A27): flip. REL041 (A25, A28): flip.

REL044 (A26, A29): before A26 before A29 (0.21); after A29 before A26 (0.235). Flip. REL045 (A26, A33): flip.

REL046 (A27, A29): flip. REL047 (A27, A33): flip.

REL048 (A28, A29): flip. REL049 (A28, A33): flip.

REL001–REL004 (A06 with A21, A22, A24, A44): A06 co-occurrence dropped from 0.30 to 0.12; A06 before B dropped from ~0.26 to ~0.055. Consistent with A06 becoming rarer.

REL005–REL011 (A19 with A20, A21, A22, A24, A25, A29, A33): before A19 before B (0.21); after B before A19 (0.15–0.16). So A19 moved from before the {A20–A25, A29, A33} group to after them. Consistent with A19's position moving later (POS002: mean 0.33 → 0.69).

LAG items: These show distance in positions between pairs.

LAG001 (A19, A29): before lag 1 (100%); after lag 5 (100%). But support after is 1 — only one observation. Weak.

LAG002 (A20, A34): before spread over lags 1–5; after lag 5 (100%). Support before 197, after 1. Weak after.

LAG003 (A22, A29): before lag 2 (support 1); after spread over lags 1–5 (support 199). So before only 1 observation.

LAG004 (A24, A34): before spread; after lag 1 (support 1). Weak.

LAG005 (A25, A29): before lag 5 (support 1); after spread (support 197).

LAG006 (A25, A34): before spread (198); after lag 5 (support 1).

LAG007 (A28, A34): before lag 4 (support 1); after lag 1 (support 41).

LAG008 (A33, A23): before lag 2 (support 1); after lag 1 (support 41).

LAG009 (A33, A24): before spread (195); after lag 3 (support 1).

LAG010 (A33, A27): before lag 3 (support 1); after lag 1 (39).

LAG011 (A33, A28): before lag 3 (1); after lag 1 (41).

LAG012 (A44, A06): before lag 1 (53); after split lag 1/5 (support 2). Weak after.

LAG013 (A44, A22): before lag 1 (support 1); after spread (192).

LAG014 (A44, A26): before lag 1 (40); after lag 4 (support 1).

LAG015 (A44, A29): before lag 2 (200); after lag 2 (support 1).

Many LAG items have very low support in one window (1 observation), so they're weak individually. But the overall pattern from DIR, POS, REL is strong.

Now, what's the overall story? Let me try to reconstruct.

Before window:
- A29 appears in all traces at mean position ~0.36 (early-ish), and many activities (A19–A28) lead to A29. A29 before A20–A25 (which sit at ~0.63). A33 at ~0.54, with A29/A20 before it? REL017: A33 before A20 (B_before_A 0.995 means A33 (B) before A20 (A)). Wait, REL017 unit is [A20, A33], A=A20, B=A33. B_before_A = 0.995 before: A33 before A20. And A33 at position 0.54, A20 at 0.635 — consistent.

So before: A19–A28 (early, ~0.31–0.36) → A29 (~0.36) → A20–A25 (~0.63) → A33 (~0.54)? Hmm, A33 at 0.54 is before A20 at 0.635. So order: early group (A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 at ~0.31–0.36), A29 (~0.36), A33 (~0.54), A20–A25 (~0.63). And A44 leads to A06, A19, A23, A26–A28 (the early group). A06 (30% participation) leads to A23, A28, A27, A19, A26.

After window:
- A34 replaces A29 as the target: A19–A28 now lead to A34. A29 moved later (0.48) and now comes after A20–A25 (which moved earlier to ~0.39). A33 moved later (0.67) and now comes after A20–A25. A44 now leads to A20–A25 group. A33 leads to A19, A23, A26–A28 group. A06 rarer (12%) and its successors changed.

So the big picture: two blocks of activities swapped their relative order. Before: block1 (A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 + A29) → A33 → block2 (A20, A21, A22, A24, A25). After: block2 (A20–A25) → A29/A33 → block1 (A19, A23, A26, A27, A28) → A34. Also A34 appears as a new successor replacing A29 for many sources.

Wait — is A34 new? DIR items show A34 as successor after; before, A34 appeared as successor of A20 (0.24), A21 (0.26), A22 (0.13), A24 (0.145), A25 (0.21). So A34 existed before as a successor of the A20–A25 group. After, A34 is the successor of A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 (nearly 100% each). And A29 was the successor of A19, A23, A26–A28 before (nearly 100% each), and after A29 is successor of A20–A25 (~0.18–0.24 each).

So it looks like the two groups swapped their downstream targets: group1 {A19, A23, A26, A27, A28} pointed to A29 before and to A34 after; group2 {A20, A21, A22, A24, A25} pointed to A34 before and to A29 after. And the positions: group2 moved earlier (0.63 → 0.39), group1 moved later (0.33 → 0.69), A29 moved later (0.36 → 0.48), A33 moved later (0.54 → 0.67).

This is consistent with a swap of two blocks: before the order was group1 → A29 → A33 → group2 (with A34 after group2 presumably); after the order is group2 → A29 → A33 → group1 → A34? Hmm, let me check: after, A20–A25 at ~0.39, A29 at 0.48, A33 at 0.67, group1 (A19, A23, A26–A28) at ~0.66–0.71. And A20–A25 lead to A29 (REL016, 022, 028, 037, 042: A20–A25 before A29 ~0.97–0.98). And group1 leads to A34 (DIR003, 007, 010–012: ~0.9–1.0 to A34). A33 after: leads to A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 (DIR013) — so A33 → group1. And A44 after leads to A20–A25 (DIR014).

Before: A44 → A06, A19, A23, A26–A28 (group1 + A06). A33 before → A20–A25 (DIR013 before: A24, A22, A25, A21, A20). A06 → A23, A28, A27, A19, A26 (group1).

So the structure before: A44 → {A06, group1} → A29 → A33 → group2 → A34 (A34 as successor of group2). After: A44 → group2 → A29 → A33 → group1 → A34.

So the hypothesis: the two activity groups {A20, A21, A22, A24, A25} and {A19, A23, A26, A27, A28} swapped their order in the process (block swap / movement of a block), with A29 and A33 staying between them, and A34 now following group1 instead of group2. Additionally A06 participation dropped.

Hmm, but wait — is it a swap of blocks, or is it that group2 moved before group1? Either way, the relational evidence directly shows order reversals between the groups: every pair (group2 member, group1 member) flipped order, and every pair (group2 member, A29/A33) flipped order.

Let me double check REL012: [A20, A23]. Before: A_only 0.77, cooccurrence 0.23, B_before_A (A23 before A20) 0.215. After: A_only 0.79, cooccurrence 0.21, A_before_B (A20 before A23) 0.21. So before A23 (group1) before A20 (group2); after A20 before A23. Flip. Good.

REL030: [A23, A24]. Before: B_only 0.77 (A24 only), cooccurrence 0.23, A_before_B (A23 before A24) 0.215. After: B_only 0.79, B_before_A (A24 before A23) 0.205. Flip. Good.

So all cross-group pairs flipped. Within-group pairs presumably unchanged (not in evidence, which suggests they didn't change enough to qualify).

Now, how to frame the main hypothesis? The evidence supports: a block of activities (A20, A21, A22, A24, A25) that previously executed after A29/A33 and after group1 (A19, A23, A26, A27, A28) now executes before them; i.e., the two blocks swapped their order. In the later window, A20–A25 run earlier (mean position ~0.39 vs ~0.63), A19/A23/A26–A28 run later (~0.66–0.71 vs ~0.31–0.36), A29 and A33 run later (~0.48 and ~0.67 vs ~0.36 and ~0.54), and the handover edges flipped: group1 now leads to A34 (which previously followed group2), and group2 now leads to A29 (which previously followed group1).

Also A06: participation dropped from 30% to 12% of traces, and its outgoing transitions changed completely. This is a separate difference (other differences).

Now, support level. Screening: 93 items vs 1.03 expected — many times larger, so chance can't explain the whole set. The hypothesis is about order/placement, which needs relational/positional evidence — we have abundant REL and POS and DIR evidence showing it directly. Consistency: all cross-group REL pairs flipped in the same direction; POS shifts agree; DIR successor changes agree (A29↔A34 handover swap). The evidence rules out "chance sampling" via the screening comparison and internal consistency.

Competing explanations: Could this be a change in path frequencies rather than a block swap? The condition for "existing paths taken with different frequencies" requires that only shares between alternatives shift, with all activities observed in substantial shares in both windows. Here participation of all main activities stays ~1.0 or similar (A20–A25 support 1.0 in both; group1 support ~0.16–0.245 in both). The order between pairs flipped from nearly fixed one direction to nearly fixed the other direction — that's a change in ordering constraints / positions, not just path frequency. Could it be that the process has two variants and the variant mix changed? E.g., before most traces followed variant X (group1 → ... → group2) and after most followed variant Y (group2 → ... → group1). That's essentially the same behavioural description at the trace level — a swap of block order. The evidence can't distinguish "the model changed" from "the mix of two existing variants flipped" — that's a competing explanation. Also, LAG items with support 1 in one window are unreliable, but the core doesn't rest on them.

Also note: A06's decline is a separate difference — participation drop (30% → 12%) and successor redistribution. Report under "Other differences".

What about A34? A34's own position isn't directly measured (no POS item for A34), but DIR shows it as successor target. Before, A34 followed group2 (A20–A25); after, it follows group1. So A34 effectively moved from after group2 to after group1 — consistent with the block swap: A34 stays at the end, and whichever group is last feeds it.

Let me also check DIR002 (A14): before 100% to A15; after 94.5% to A15 plus small others. Observed change tiny (0.00037) — this is a trivially small change that still qualified (empirical strength high but observed_change minuscule). I should not emphasize it; it's a minor item. Actually its observed_change is 0.00037 — negligible. It's one of the 93 items but describes essentially no change. I can ignore or briefly note. Better not to list every minor component. I'll skip it.

DIR015 (A49): before 99% to A50; after 94.5% to A50 plus small others. Change 0.00045 — negligible. Skip.

Now the main hypothesis statement: "In the later window, the block A20, A21, A22, A24, A25 executes earlier and the block A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 executes later — the two blocks swapped their order around A29 and A33."

Let me quantify:
- POS: A20 mean position 0.64 → 0.39; A21 0.64 → 0.39; A22 0.63 → 0.40; A24 0.63 → 0.39; A25 0.63 → 0.40. Group1: A19 0.33 → 0.69; A23 0.36 → 0.68; A26 0.31 → 0.66; A27 0.33 → 0.71; A28 0.34 → 0.70. A29 0.36 → 0.48; A33 0.54 → 0.67.
- REL: e.g., A29 before A20 in about 995 in 1000 traces before; A20 before A29 in about 98 in 100 after (REL016). Similar for A21, A22, A24, A25 with A29 and A33 (REL017, 022, 023, 028, 029, 037, 038, 042, 043).
- Cross-group: A23 before A20 in ~21.5% of traces before (co-occurring ones) → A20 before A23 in ~21% after (REL012); similar for many pairs.
- DIR: A19: 100% → A29 before, 91% → A34 after (DIR003); A23: 96% → A29 before, 98% → A34 after (DIR007); A26: 93% → A29 before, 90% → A34 after (DIR010); A27: 98% → A29 before, 100% → A34 after (DIR011); A28: 97% → A29 before, 98% → A34 after (DIR012).
